correctness.rationale: Conservation of Q follows exactly from the ODE, and H=(1-Q)/2 gives the Hamiltonian orientation. Each noncritical level 0<Q<1 is a simple closed orbit; a quarter-orbit integral yields T=4K(sqrt(1-Q)) in original physical time. Independent uniform coordinates give density f_U(u)=1/(2sqrt(1-u)), and multiplicative convolution f_Q(q)=K(sqrt(1-q))/2. The elliptic E/K derivative identity integrates to the stated CDF with endpoints 0 and 1. Complementary-modulus expansion K=L+O(qL), E=1+q(L-1/2)/2+O(q^2L) gives q_t=16e^(-t/2)(1+O(t e^(-t/2))) and the stated two-term tail; the nonnegative layer-cake identity gives sharp moment threshold including divergence at equality. Independently evaluated q=.2,10^-4,10^-9 and ratios to two-term tail 1.1301,1.00024,1.000000005, supporting but not proving asymptotics.

value.rationale: PASS: uniform initialization in a two-strategy state square defines a natural full-dimensional ensemble; its period tail determines precisely how common long transient cycles are. The multiplicative t prefactor, explicit constant term and sharp exponential-moment boundary quantify separatrix slowdown in a way not supplied by a known orbit-by-orbit period integral. This is a motivated exact distribution, not an arbitrary numerical slice.

final_claim: For dot X=(1-X^2)Y, dot Y=-(1-Y^2)X with initial point area-uniform on (-1,1)^2, Q=(1-X^2)(1-Y^2) has CDF 1-E(sqrt(1-q))+q K(sqrt(1-q)); T=4K(sqrt(1-Q)), with P(T>t)=(2t+4)e^(-t/2)+O(t^2 e^-t), critical exponential moment s=1/2.
